mechanism_caveat: Both issuers in this run are backed by Touchstone's own API accounts. Issuer credit risk — the thing that makes a work claim an instrument rather than a gift card — is absent by construction. This run proves mechanism, not demand, and no result from it is evidence that a third-party issuer would behave the same way.
f2_caveat: And on F2 specifically: because both issuers are Touchstone-backed, a forward issued here cannot default. HEDGER therefore tests price-risk transfer only, not credit-risk transfer, which is the easier half. "The forward worked" must never be read as "the forward survives an issuer failing."
